title: Two clocks
html:
This is the last picture camera CAM-04 stored before it went dark.

Exhibit PDU/05cam04_204055.jpgthe last picture CAM-04 stored before it went darkDownload
CameraRoomTime on the pictureWhat it shows
CAM-04Salle des Etats20:40:55The Mona Lisa on its easel, crate CR-017 open beside it
CAM-02Service corridor20:40:08Crate CR-017 covered, on a trolley

The crate cannot be covered in the corridor before it stands open in the gallery. So one of the two camera clocks is wrong.

The museum knew that one camera clock was off. Somebody wrote it down, in a file you got in stage 1.

Every camera has its own clock. The door log and the system log both use the museum's central clock, and that one is right.

prev_card.title: You traced the dark camera
prev_card.html:
WS-02 switched off CAM-04 at 20:41:08. WS-02 is the desk of Julien Moreau. That does not yet prove he sat there: anyone at WS-02 could have used it.

system_log.json is JSON: every event is a set of key-value pairs between curly brackets, and the whole file is a list of events. A login has "target": null: there is no value.

fields.label: Which camera's clock is wrong? Give its ID.
What was the real time, on the central clock, when the covered crate passed the corridor camera?
Going by that real time: whose badge opened the door to the service corridor closest to it? Give the name of that person.

hints: Read incident_report.txt again, to the end.

Read the last section of incident_report.txt, OPEN MAINTENANCE NOTES. It names the camera and how many minutes it is behind. Add that to the time on the corridor still. Then, in door_log.csv, find the corridor swipe closest to that new time, as in stage 4.
